# Introduction

This interactive R notebook provides a workflow for quality assurance and
quality control (QA/QC) of GEO-TREES tree inventory data. 

This notebook is provided as both a `.qmd` Quarto file, which we recommend
running in RStudio, and as a `.ipynb` Jupyter Notebook, which you can run in
JupyterLab either locally or on the ESA/NASA MAAP platforms. You can use either
version to QA/QC your data.

Each GEO-TREES acquisition contains one census of each plot, the __focal
census__, within a single site. The focal census is processed by the 
[GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing) 
to estimate above-ground woody biomass density (AGBD). The focal census should
normally be the census closest in time either before or after to the airborne
LiDAR (ALS) acquisition. If you have data from other censuses of the same
plots, they can also be included in this QC workflow. Data from other censuses
are not used for GEO-TREES biomass estimation, but they can be useful for
finding errors in the focal census, e.g. implausible diameter growth, stems
which were missed, or taxonomic names which differ from previous censuses.

The notebook has two parts:

* [Part I](#part-i-focal-census-checks) checks the focal census on its own, 
  and previews how the GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline will use it.
* [Part II](#part-ii-multi-census-checks-of-the-focal-census) compares the 
  focal census to other censuses, to highlight issues affecting the 
  focal census.

The process for QA/QC:

1. Create a copy of your raw stem measurement data that conforms to the
   GEO-TREES L0 data format. See the [GEO-TREES Tree Inventory Guidelines, _Section 16: Data format_](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q5Wy_LbNEa0tNaGVntL0Bku41Z3t-TeU85_IxZuC6Uc/edit?usp=sharing). 
2. Open this notebook and load your __copy__ of the L0 tree inventory data.
3. Run the code chunks interactively in the notebook. Look at the outputs, and
   make changes to the input data where necessary. Changes can be made either
   by adding code to the notebook, or manually editing your __copy__ of the L0
   tree inventory data. 
4. Once you have finished working through the notebook, save and render the
   notebook as a HTML file. Note that all code in the notebook must run without
   errors for the file to render successfully. The method depends on whether
   you are using the `.qmd` or `.ipynb` version:
    * `.qmd` in RStudio: Run `quarto::quarto_render("INV_quality_control_nb.qmd",
      output_format = "html")` in the R console. You may need to run
      `install.packages("quarto")` first.
    * `.ipynb` in JupyterLab: Click `File > Save and Export Notebook As > HTML`
5. Send the following data to GEO-TREES for data archiving:
    * Original version of the raw data
    * Formatted raw data in the GEO-TREES L0 data format
    * Raw data with changes made following QA/QC, if fixes were applied manually.
    * The focal census stem measurement table written at the end of this
      notebook, `stem_focal.csv`
    * The completed `.qmd` / `.ipynb` QA/QC notebook
    * Rendered HTML of the QA/QC notebook 

# Setup

Install and load the GEO-TREES tree inventory QA/QC R package contained in this repository. This package
contains various convenience functions for flagging and optionally correcting
tree inventory data. The package will also load other packages as
dependencies. If you want to load additional packages to help you explore and
manipulate your tree inventory data, you can add to the code chunk below.

```{r}
#| eval: false
devtools::install_github("GEO-TREES/INV_quality_control")
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(treeInvQC)
library(BIOMASS)  # Match taxonomic names to WFO `correctTaxo()`, fit diameter-height models `modelHD()`, wood density `getWoodDensity()`, AGB `computeAGB()`
library(DT)  # Pretty tables in HTML notebooks
library(ggplot2)  # Plots
library(tibble)  # `tribble()` - create dataframes by row
```

```{r}
theme_set(theme_bw())  # Set default ggplot2 theme
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# DO NOT EDIT
# Change default displayHelp rendering if compiled as HTML
if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) {
  formals(displayHelp)$html <- TRUE
} 
```

Throughout the notebook we display the help files for different functions
using the `displayHelp()` function. Below is the help file for
the `treeInvQC` R package:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(treeInvQC)
```

## Create L0 tree inventory data   

Create a __copy__ of your raw stem measurement data that conforms to the GEO-TREES 
L0 data format. See the [GEO-TREES Tree Inventory Guidelines, _Section 16: Data format_](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q5Wy_LbNEa0tNaGVntL0Bku41Z3t-TeU85_IxZuC6Uc/edit?usp=sharing). 
__The original raw data should not be altered, always work with a copy of the data__.

You can use the [ATFS Data Harmonization Shiny app](https://github.com/Alliance-for-Tropical-Forest-Science/DataHarmonization) 
to help re-format your stem measurement data if you wish. The `inst/` folder in
[this repository](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_quality_control) 
contains a `.rds` output profile for the GEO-TREES data format, which you can
load into the app. The app will walk you through creating an input profile for
your data, then performs the re-formatting procedure.

Alternatively, you can manually re-format your data, for example using a
spreadsheet editor, or in R.

The QA/QC code below requires you to supply the stem measurement table, the
plot meta-data table, and the plot geo-location table. 

You can also optionally provide a taxonomy table, stem height measurement
table, and wood density measurement table.

## Load data

Edit the code below to load your tree inventory data in the GEO-TREES L0 data
format.

The example data loaded below are from the Bicuar site in Angola. Known errors
have been added to the example data by `bicuar_test_data/02_add_errors.R`, so
that the checks in this notebook have issues to find. The errors which were
added are listed in `bicuar_test_data/out_errors/errors_added.csv`.

Load stem measurement table, including all censuses of each plot:

```{r}
s <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out_errors/stem.csv")
```

Load plot meta-data table:

```{r}
p <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out_errors/plot.csv")
```

Load plot geo-location table:

```{r}
pt <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out_errors/plot_pt.csv")
```

Optionally load taxonomy table:

```{r}
#| eval: false
tx <- read.csv("taxon_example.csv")
```

Optionally load additional stem height data:

```{r}
#| eval: false
h <- read.csv("height_example.csv")
```

Optionally load additional wood density data:

```{r}
#| eval: false
wd <- read.csv("wood_density_example.csv")
```

Optionally load a table of subplot boundaries:

```{r}
subs <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out_errors/subplot.csv")
```

Columns which uniquely identify each stem measurement, stem, tree,
and plot are used by many checks below.

With multi-census data, stem measurements must include the census ID
(`census_id`), which identifies the census of each plot. The order of censuses
is taken from `census_id`, so values must be integers which increase with each
census of a plot, e.g. `1`, `2`, `3`. 

```{r}
id_meas <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "census_id", "tree_id", "stem_id", "measurement_id")
id_stem <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "tree_id", "stem_id")
id_tree <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "tree_id")
id_plot <- c("site_id", "plot_id")
```

## Focal census

Choose the focal census of each plot, e.g. the census closest to the ALS
acquisition that will be provided to GEO-TREES for biomass estimation. Provide
a dataframe to `focal`, with one row per plot, specifying the `census_id` for
each plot. The notebook stops if a plot has more than one focal census, or if a
focal census is not in the stem measurement table.

```{r}
# Focal census of each plot. Edit for your data
focal <- tribble(
  ~site_id, ~plot_id, ~census_id,
  "Bicuar", "B1",     1,
  "Bicuar", "B2",     1,
  "Bicuar", "M2",     2,
  "Bicuar", "M3",     2,
  "Bicuar", "O1",     1,
  "Bicuar", "O2",     1,
  "Bicuar", "P2",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P3",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P4",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P5",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P6",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P7",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P8",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P9",     3,
  "Bicuar", "P10",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P11",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P12",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P13",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P14",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P15",    3,
  "Bicuar", "P16",    2
)
```

```{r}
# Each plot must have only one focal census
if (any(duplicated(focal[, id_plot]))) {
  stop("Plots with more than one focal census in `focal`")
}

# Each focal census must be in the stem measurement table
focal_key <- paste(focal$site_id, focal$plot_id, focal$census_id)
s_key <- paste(s$site_id, s$plot_id, s$census_id)
if (!all(focal_key %in% s_key)) {
  stop("Focal censuses not in the stem measurement table: ",
    paste(setdiff(focal_key, s_key), collapse = ", "))
}

s$focal <- s_key %in% focal_key

# Plots without a focal census are not checked in Part I of this notebook
plot_none <- setdiff(unique(paste(s$site_id, s$plot_id)),
  paste(focal$site_id, focal$plot_id))
if (length(plot_none) > 0) {
  message("Plots without a focal census: ", paste(plot_none, collapse = ", "))
}

message(sum(s$focal), " measurements in the focal census of ",
  nrow(unique(s[s$focal, id_plot])), " plots")

# Stem measurements in the focal census
s_focal <- s[s$focal, ]
```

Visualise the census timeline of each plot.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
cens <- unique(s[, c("plot_id", "census_id", "census_date", "focal")])

# Convert census dates to decimal years
cens$census_date_dec <- decYear(cens$census_date)

ggplot(cens, aes(x = census_date_dec, y = plot_id)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = plot_id), colour = "grey") + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 3) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  labs(x = "Census date", y = "Plot", fill = "Focal census")
```

## Thresholds

The thresholds used by the checks below are defined here, so that they can be
adjusted in one place for your forest type and measurement protocols. The
defaults are suitable for most tropical forests. The INV_processing
parameters should match the parameters in `param.yaml` which will be used to
process your data.

```{r}
# Plausible ranges of measurements
diam_max_cm <- 200  # Maximum stem diameter (cm)
height_max_m <- 50  # Maximum stem height (m)
pom_tol_m <- 0.05  # Tolerance when comparing the average POM of stems to the plot default (m)

# Outliers and measurement precision
height_resid_max <- 3  # Maximum height-diameter model residual (residual SDs)
ba_share_max <- 0.05  # Maximum proportion of plot basal area in one stem
unit_ratio_max <- 5  # Maximum ratio between plot mean diameter and the median of all plots
diam_cv_max <- 100  # Maximum coefficient of variation of diameter in a plot (%)
round_prop_max <- 0.3  # Maximum proportion of diameters which are whole numbers of cm
digit_prop_max <- 0.15  # Maximum proportion of diameters with the same terminal digit

# Measurement dates
als_date <- NULL  # Date of the matching ALS acquisition, e.g. "2024-03"
date_diff_max_yr <- 1  # Maximum difference between measurement dates and `als_date` (decimal years)
date_span_max_yr <- 1  # Maximum spread of measurement dates within a plot (decimal years)

# Stem locations and trees
outside_tol_m <- 0  # Distance a stem can be outside the plot boundary (m)
subplot_tol_m <- 1  # Distance a stem can be outside its subplot (m)
tree_stem_dist_max_m <- 5  # Maximum distance between stems of a tree (m)
tree_stem_max <- 12  # Maximum number of stems per tree

# Changes between censuses
change_ann_max <- 0.05  # Maximum annual relative change in plot totals (%, e.g. 5%)
change_ann_max_subplot <- 0.1  # Maximum annual relative change in subplot totals (%, e.g. 10%)
demog_rate_max <- 0.05  # Maximum annual mortality or recruitment rate
tag_dist_max_m <- 1  # Maximum distance between a recruit and a disappeared stem (m)
tag_diam_tol <- 0.1  # Maximum relative difference in diameter of a retagged stem
growth_min_cm_yr <- -2  # Minimum annual diameter growth (cm)
growth_max_cm_yr <- 4  # Maximum annual diameter growth (cm)
recruit_growth_max_cm_yr <- 5  # Maximum annual diameter growth of recruits (cm)
loc_change_max_m <- 2  # Maximum change in stem location between censuses (m)

# INV_processing parameters, see `param.yaml`
inv_missing_diam_impute <- TRUE  # `missing_diam_method: "impute"`
inv_include_broken <- TRUE  # `include_broken`
inv_agbd_diam_min_cm <- 0  # `agbd_diam_min_cm`
inv_growth_form_exclude <- NULL  # `growth_form_exclude`
```

Tables of flagged records are shown with the function below, which shows a
message instead of an empty table if no records are flagged:

```{r}
showFlags <- function(x) {
  if (NROW(x) == 0) {
    message("No records flagged")
  } else {
    datatable(as.data.frame(x))
  }
}
```

# Part I: Focal census checks

The checks in this part of the notebook use only the focal census, `s_focal`, which will be
submitted to the GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline.

## Data format 

### Check table columns

`checkTableSpec()` checks your data against the column specifications in the
[INV_processing templates](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/tree/main/templates) 
and reports any issues. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(checkTableSpec)
```


Rows with `severity` "error" must be fixed before the data can be processed.
Rows with `severity` "warning" can be fixed by coercing the column to the
correct class, e.g. `s$subplot_id <- as.character(s$subplot_id)`.

```{r}
# `allow_extra = TRUE` allows columns which are useful during QA/QC, e.g.
# `census_id`. Only the columns in the specification are written to the focal
# census stem table at the end of this notebook
df_checkTableSpec_stem <- checkTableSpec(s_focal, "stem", allow_extra = TRUE)
showFlags(df_checkTableSpec_stem)
```

Check the plot meta-data table in the same way:

```{r}
df_checkTableSpec_plot <- checkTableSpec(p, "plot")
showFlags(df_checkTableSpec_plot)
```

Check the plot geo-location table in the same way:

```{r}
df_checkTableSpec_pt <- checkTableSpec(pt, "pt")
showFlags(df_checkTableSpec_pt)
```

### Matching IDs among tables

Every plot in the stem measurement table must be in the plot meta-data table,
and every plot in the plot meta-data table must have geo-location points:

```{r}
# Plots in the stem table which are missing from the plot table
df_plotMissing <- setdiff(unique(s_focal$plot_id), p$plot_id)
showFlags(df_plotMissing)

# Plots in the plot table which are missing from the geo-location table
df_ptMissing <- setdiff(p$plot_id, pt$plot_id)
showFlags(df_ptMissing)
```

If you have provided optional tables, check that they match the stem table.
Every taxonomic name in the stem table must be in the taxonomy table:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Every taxonomic name in the stem table must be in the taxonomy table
df_taxonMissing <- setdiff(unique(s_focal$taxon_name), tx$taxon_name)
showFlags(df_taxonMissing)
```

Wood density measurements of taxa which are not in the stem table are not
used by INV_processing:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Wood density measurements of taxa not in the stem table are not used
df_wdMissing <- setdiff(wd$taxon_name, s_focal$taxon_name)
showFlags(df_wdMissing)
```

## Missing, duplicated, and phantom records

### Duplicated records

Duplicated records should be merged or removed. There should only be one
measurement for each concatenation of
`site_id`+`plot_id`+`census_id`+`tree_id`+`stem_id`+`measurement_id`.

```{r}
# Measurement records with duplicated ID values
df_recordDup <- s_focal[duplicated(s_focal[, id_meas]), id_meas]
showFlags(df_recordDup)
```

### Missing values

Some columns must never contain `<NA>` values, particularly ID values. 

```{r}
# Columns which must never be empty
cols_req <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "tree_id", "stem_id", "census_id", 
  "measurement_date", "taxon_name", "code")
is_empty <- is.na(s_focal[, cols_req]) | s_focal[, cols_req] == ""
df_valMissing <- s_focal[rowSums(is_empty, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, c(id_meas, cols_req)]

showFlags(df_valMissing)
```

Some columns are only allowed to contain missing values under certain
conditions. For example, living and standing stems should always have a
diameter measurement. 

```{r}
# Live stems without a diameter, which are not fallen, missing, or broken 
# below the POM
df_diamMissing <- s_focal[is.na(s_focal$diam_cm) & grepl("A", s_focal$code) & 
  !grepl("[TFM]", s_focal$code), c(id_meas, "code", "diam_cm")]

showFlags(df_diamMissing)
```

If a stem has a diameter measurement then it should have a Point of Measurement (POM) value.

```{r}
# Stems with a diameter but no POM
df_pomMissing <- s_focal[!is.na(s_focal$diam_cm) & is.na(s_focal$pom_m), 
  c(id_meas, "diam_cm", "pom_m")]

showFlags(df_pomMissing)
```


### Values which should be empty

Missing stems ("M") should not have diameter measurements, POM
or height measurement. Stems broken below the POM ("T") should not have 
diameter measurements:

```{r}
# Stems recorded as missing ("M") with a diameter, POM or height
df_valPresentMissing <- s_focal[grepl("M", s_focal$code) & 
  (!is.na(s_focal$diam_cm) | !is.na(s_focal$pom_m) | !is.na(s_focal$height_m)), 
  c(id_meas, "code", "diam_cm", "pom_m", "height_m")]

showFlags(df_valPresentMissing)

# Stems broken below the POM ("T") with a diameter
df_diamBroken <- s_focal[grepl("T", s_focal$code) & !is.na(s_focal$diam_cm), 
  c(id_meas, "code", "diam_cm")]

showFlags(df_diamBroken)
```

## Diameter and height measurements

Inspect the distribution of diameter measurements. Are all measurements larger
than the minimum diameter threshold of the plot? Are any measurements
unrealistically large? 

```{r}
# Plot a histogram
ggplot(s_focal[!is.na(s_focal$diam_cm), ], aes(x = diam_cm)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, colour = "black", fill = "grey") + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of stems")

# Summarise values
summary(s_focal$diam_cm)
```

Diameter distributions in natural forests normally decline steeply from the
minimum diameter threshold. Look for plots where the smallest diameter class
has fewer stems than the next, which may mean that small stems were missed,
or that the threshold in the plot meta-data table is wrong. Plotting on a log
scale makes the large stems, which dominate AGB, easier to see.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
diam_min <- p[, c("plot_id", "meas_diam_min_cm")]

ggplot(s_focal[!is.na(s_focal$diam_cm), ], aes(x = diam_cm)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, boundary = 0, fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  geom_vline(data = diam_min, aes(xintercept = meas_diam_min_cm), 
    colour = "red", linetype = 2) + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of stems")
```

Compare the diameter distribution of live stems in the focal census to other
censuses of the same plot. The distributions should be similar, unless there
has been a major disturbance:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
ggplot(s[grepl("A", s$code) & !is.na(s$diam_cm), ], 
  aes(x = diam_cm, colour = factor(census_id), linewidth = focal)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 1.2, "FALSE" = 0.4)) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of live stems", 
    colour = "Census", linewidth = "Focal census")
```

Live stems should be at or above the minimum diameter threshold of their plot,
`meas_diam_min_cm` in the plot meta-data table. Stems below the minimum
diameter threshold have their own AGB estimate in INV_processing, but are not
included in AGB density. Many stems below the threshold may indicate that the
threshold in the plot meta-data table is wrong, or that diameters are in the
wrong units:

```{r}
# Live stems below the minimum diameter threshold of their plot
diam_min_cm <- p$meas_diam_min_cm[match(s_focal$plot_id, p$plot_id)]
df_diamMin <- cbind(s_focal[, c(id_meas, "diam_cm")], diam_min_cm)[
  which(grepl("A", s_focal$code) & s_focal$diam_cm < diam_min_cm), ]

showFlags(df_diamMin)
```

Diameters must be greater than 0 in INV_processing, and diameters greater than
`diam_max_cm` are very rare:

```{r}
# Diameters outside a plausible range (cm)
df_diamRange <- s_focal[which(s_focal$diam_cm <= 0 | s_focal$diam_cm > diam_max_cm), c(id_meas, "diam_cm")]

showFlags(df_diamRange)
```

### Large stems

A single data entry error in the diameter of a large stem can change plot AGB
density more than errors in many small stems. Stems with more than
`ba_share_max` of the basal area of live stems in their plot are listed
below. Check that the diameters of the largest stems in each plot are
correct:

```{r}
ba <- ifelse(grepl("A", s_focal$code) & !is.na(s_focal$diam_cm), s_focal$diam_cm^2, 0)
ba_share <- ba / ave(ba, s_focal$plot_id, FUN = sum)
df_bigStem <- cbind(s_focal[, c(id_meas, "diam_cm")], ba_share)[ba_share > ba_share_max, ]
df_bigStem <- df_bigStem[order(-df_bigStem$ba_share), ]

showFlags(df_bigStem)
```

### Height measurements

If height measurements are available, find potentially erroneous measurements
based on the relationship between height and diameter measurements. Heights 
are often not measured in every census, so height measurements from all
censuses are used to fit the height-diameter model. If you have provided a
separate height table, `h`, you can fit the model to those data instead.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagModOutlier)
```

```{r}
# Fit a simple height-diameter model using the BIOMASS package, using height
# measurements from all censuses
s_h <- s[!is.na(s$height_m) & !is.na(s$diam_cm), ]

hmod <- BIOMASS::modelHD(
  D = s_h$diam_cm, 
  H = s_h$height_m,
  method = "weibull",
  bayesian = FALSE,
  drawGraph = FALSE)

# Flag outlier measurements using model residuals
df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all <- flagModOutlier(
  x = s_h, 
  meas_id = id_meas,
  mod = hmod$model, 
  x_var = "diam_cm",
  y_var = "height_m",
  threshold = height_resid_max,
  comment = "Height-diameter model outlier"
)

showFlags(df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all)

# Outliers in the focal census
df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm <- merge(
  df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all, unique(s_focal[, id_meas]))
```

Plot heights against diameters, with the fitted model, and the outliers
highlighted. These outliers are not necessarily errors, but do deserve closer
inspection:

```{r}
s_hd <- merge(s_h, df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all[, c(id_meas, "comment")], 
  all.x = TRUE)
s_hd$outlier <- !is.na(s_hd$comment)
hd_line <- data.frame(diam_cm = seq(min(s_h$diam_cm), max(s_h$diam_cm), 
  length.out = 100))
hd_line$height_m <- predict(hmod$model, newdata = data.frame(D = hd_line$diam_cm))

ggplot(s_hd, aes(x = diam_cm, y = height_m)) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = outlier), alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_line(data = hd_line) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey50")) + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Stem height (m)", colour = "Model outlier")
```

Heights must be greater than 0 in INV_processing, and heights greater than
`height_max_m` are rare:

```{r}
# Heights outside a plausible range (m)
df_heightRange <- s_focal[which(s_focal$height_m <= 0 | s_focal$height_m > height_max_m), 
  c(id_meas, "height_m")]

showFlags(df_heightRange)
```

## Measurement precision

### Unit mixtures

Diameters recorded in the wrong units, e.g. in mm rather than cm, give very
wrong AGB estimates. Plots where the mean diameter is more than
`unit_ratio_max` times larger or smaller than the median of all plots may be
in the wrong units. Plots where diameters are very variable, with a
coefficient of variation (%) greater than `diam_cv_max`, may contain a mix of
units:

```{r}
# Mean and coefficient of variation (%) of diameter in each plot
diam_summ <- aggregate(diam_cm ~ plot_id, data = s_focal, 
  FUN = function(i) { c(mean = mean(i), cv = 100 * sd(i) / mean(i)) })
diam_summ <- do.call(data.frame, diam_summ)
names(diam_summ) <- c("plot_id", "diam_mean", "diam_cv")

diam_mean_all <- median(diam_summ$diam_mean)
df_valUnit <- diam_summ[
  diam_summ$diam_mean > unit_ratio_max * diam_mean_all | 
  diam_summ$diam_mean < diam_mean_all / unit_ratio_max | 
  diam_summ$diam_cv > diam_cv_max, ]

showFlags(df_valUnit)
```

### Rounded values

If diameters are measured to the nearest mm, about 10% should be whole
numbers of cm. A much higher proportion implies poor measurement precision.
Plots where the proportion of diameters which are whole numbers of cm is
greater than `round_prop_max` are listed below:

```{r}
df_valRound <- aggregate(diam_cm ~ plot_id, data = s_focal, 
  FUN = function(i) { mean(i == round(i)) })
names(df_valRound)[2] <- "prop_round"
df_valRound <- df_valRound[df_valRound$prop_round > round_prop_max, ]

showFlags(df_valRound)
```

### Terminal digit preference

An excess of terminal digits 0 and 5 suggests that diameters were estimated
or rounded, rather than read from the tape. This increases diameter
measurement error, and may indicate that some stems were not measured.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValDigit)
```

```{r}
df_flagValDigit_diam_cm <- flagValDigit(
  x = s_focal,
  group_id = "plot_id",
  target = "diam_cm",
  digits = 1,
  max_prop = digit_prop_max,
  comment = "Terminal digit preference in diameter"
)

showFlags(df_flagValDigit_diam_cm)
```

Plot the proportion of diameters ending in each digit, in each plot. The
dashed line shows the expected proportion if digits are uniformly
distributed:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
digit <- data.frame(
  plot_id = s_focal$plot_id, 
  digit = factor(round(s_focal$diam_cm * 10) %% 10))
digit <- digit[!is.na(digit$digit), ]

ggplot(digit, aes(x = digit)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = 1), fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1, linetype = 2) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Terminal digit of diameter (mm)", y = "Proportion of stems")
```

## Point of measurement (POM)

Inspect the distribution of POM values. Most stems should be measured at the
default POM of the plot, `meas_pom_default_m` in the plot meta-data table,
normally 1.3 m:

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(s_focal[!is.na(s_focal$pom_m), ], aes(x = pom_m)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0, fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(x = "POM (m)", y = "Number of stems")
```

INV_processing can correct diameters measured above 1.3 m to their equivalent
at 1.3 m using a taper model. Stems measured above the default POM because of
buttresses should have the "U" code, and stems measured away from the default
POM because of irregularities should have the "I" code.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPomDefault)
```

```{r}
df_flagPomDefault <- flagPomDefault(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  pom = "pom_m",
  code = "code",
  plot = p,
  plot_pom_default = "meas_pom_default_m",
  code_raised = c("U", "I"),
  tol = pom_tol_m,
  comment = "POM inconsistent with plot default"
)

showFlags(df_flagPomDefault)
```

Plot POM against diameter. Stems measured above the default POM are normally
large, buttressed stems:

```{r}
ggplot(s_focal[!is.na(s_focal$pom_m) & !is.na(s_focal$diam_cm), ], 
  aes(x = diam_cm, y = pom_m, colour = grepl("[UI]", code))) + 
  geom_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.02, alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_hline(data = p, aes(yintercept = meas_pom_default_m), linetype = 2) + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "POM (m)", colour = "Raised POM code")
```

## Stem condition codes

`flagCodeVal()` identifies measurements either with invalid values in the
`code` column, or invalid combinations or codes. For example, a stem cannot be
dead ("D") and alive ("A") at the same time, or standing ("S") and fallen
("F"). INV_processing stops if any of these are found. The valid codes are
described in the [INV_processing templates](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/blob/main/templates/stem_codes.csv).

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagCodeVal)
```

```{r}
df_flagCodeVal <- flagCodeVal(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "code",
  accepted = c("A", "D", "S", "F", "M", "B", "T", "U", "I", "H"),
  invalid_comb = list(
	c("A", "D"),
	c("S", "F"),
	c("B", "T")
  ),
  cond = NULL,
  comment = "Invalid code values"
)

showFlags(df_flagCodeVal)
```

A stem which was not found ("M") cannot have its condition recorded. Only
"A" or "D" can be combined with "M", e.g. "AM" for a stem known to be alive,
but which was not found during this census:

```{r}
df_flagCodeVal_missing <- flagCodeVal(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "code",
  invalid_comb = list(
	c("M", "S"),
	c("M", "F"),
	c("M", "B"),
	c("M", "T"),
	c("M", "U"),
	c("M", "I"),
	c("M", "H")
  ),
  comment = "Condition codes on missing stem"
)

showFlags(df_flagCodeVal_missing)
```

Every code must record whether the stem is alive or dead ("A" or "D"), and,
unless the stem was not found ("M"), whether it is standing or fallen ("S" or
"F"). INV_processing only includes stems with both "A" and "S" in AGB
estimates, and excludes stems broken below the POM ("T") or not found ("M").
A live, standing stem whose code is missing "A" or "S" is excluded from AGB
estimates without a warning:

```{r}
# Codes without a mortality status, or without a standing status
df_codeIncomplete <- s_focal[!grepl("[AD]", s_focal$code) | 
  (!grepl("[SF]", s_focal$code) & !grepl("M", s_focal$code)), c(id_meas, "code")]

showFlags(df_codeIncomplete)
```

## Measurement dates

GEO-TREES acquisitions should contain one census per plot, which should
generally be within one year of the corresponding airborne LiDAR acquisition.
Set `als_date` in [Thresholds](#thresholds) to check this. Measurement dates spread over a long
period within one plot may indicate that measurements from more than one 
census have been mixed.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagMeasDate)
```

```{r}
df_flagMeasDate <- flagMeasDate(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  date = "measurement_date",
  ref_date = als_date,
  max_diff = date_diff_max_yr,
  max_span = date_span_max_yr,
  comment = "Suspect measurement date"
)

showFlags(df_flagMeasDate)
```

Plot the range of measurement dates in the focal census of each plot:

```{r}
ggplot(s_focal, aes(x = decYear(measurement_date), y = plot_id)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 1) + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(i) sprintf("%.2f", i)) + 
  labs(x = "Measurement date (decimal year)", y = "Plot")
```

## Stem coordinate issues

Inspect the spatial distribution of stems within each plot. Are any stems
outside the plot, or distributed unevenly within the plot?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
# Plot stem coordinates, sized by diameter
ggplot(s_focal, aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m, size = diam_cm)) + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, colour = "grey30", na.rm = TRUE) + 
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4) + 
  coord_equal() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "X (m)", y = "Y (m)", size = "Diameter (cm)")
```

### Stems outside the plot

Stems outside the quadrat grid of their plot are excluded from quadrat AGB
density estimates by INV_processing, unless they are within
`outside_max_dist_m` of a quadrat.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagStemOutside)
```

```{r}
df_flagStemOutside <- flagStemOutside(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  pt = pt,
  tol = outside_tol_m,
  comment = "Stem outside plot boundary"
)

showFlags(df_flagStemOutside)
```

Map stems outside the plot boundary:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
sf_out <- merge(s_focal, df_flagStemOutside[, c(id_meas, "comment")], all.x = TRUE)
sf_out$outside <- !is.na(sf_out$comment)
sf_out <- sf_out[order(sf_out$outside), ]

ggplot(sf_out, aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m, colour = outside)) + 
  geom_point(size = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey70")) + 
  coord_equal() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "X (m)", y = "Y (m)", colour = "Outside plot")
```

### Stem coordinates relative to subplots

If you have loaded a table of field subplot boundaries, `subs`, check that
stems are located inside their labelled subplot. If you do not have a table
of subplot boundaries, add `#| eval: false` to the code chunks below, so that
they are not run when the notebook is rendered.

`correctLocSub()` checks whether XY coordinates match with subplot coordinates
and optionally re-locates incongruously located stems to the center of their
subplot. Stems without coordinates are excluded, as they are not located
outside their subplot. If `correct = TRUE`, stems outside their subplot are
given the coordinates of the centre of the subplot. In INV_processing, trees
without coordinates are placed at random within the extent of their subplot,
so stems with wrong coordinates or subplot IDs affect AGB density estimates.

```{r}
# Results are empty if no subplot table is provided
df_correctLocSub <- NULL
```

Check the subplot table against the INV_processing specification:

```{r}
df_checkTableSpec_subs <- checkTableSpec(subs, "subplot")
showFlags(df_checkTableSpec_subs)
```

Map the subplots over the stems, to check that subplots tile each plot
without overlapping:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
# Stems in plots with subplot boundaries
s_sub <- s_focal[s_focal$plot_id %in% subs$plot_id, ]

ggplot(s_sub, aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m)) +
  geom_rect(data = subs,
    aes(xmin = x_rel_min_m, xmax = x_rel_max_m, ymin = y_rel_min_m, ymax = y_rel_max_m),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(subplot_id)), size = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_equal() +
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "X (m)", y = "Y (m)")
```

Check whether stems are inside their labelled subplot, allowing a tolerance
of `subplot_tol_m`, and suggest corrected coordinates at the centre of the subplot:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctLocSub)
```

```{r}
df_correctLocSub <- correctLocSub(
  x = s_sub[!is.na(s_sub$x_rel_m) & !is.na(s_sub$y_rel_m), ],
  meas_id = id_meas,
  subplot_id = c("plot_id", "subplot_id"),
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  subs = subs,
  subs_subplot_id = c("plot_id", "subplot_id"),
  subs_x_min = "x_rel_min_m",
  subs_x_max = "x_rel_max_m",
  subs_y_min = "y_rel_min_m",
  subs_y_max = "y_rel_max_m",
  tol = subplot_tol_m,
  correct = TRUE,
  comment = "Stem coordinates outside subplot"
)

showFlags(df_correctLocSub)
```

Map stems outside their subplot:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
sf_sub <- merge(s_sub, df_correctLocSub[, c(id_meas, "comment")], all.x = TRUE)
sf_sub$outside <- !is.na(sf_sub$comment)
sf_sub <- sf_sub[order(sf_sub$outside), ]

ggplot(sf_sub, aes(x = x_rel_m, y = y_rel_m)) +
  geom_rect(data = subs,
    aes(xmin = x_rel_min_m, xmax = x_rel_max_m, ymin = y_rel_min_m, ymax = y_rel_max_m),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = outside), size = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey70")) +
  coord_equal() +
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) +
  labs(x = "X (m)", y = "Y (m)", colour = "Outside subplot")
```

### Trees without coordinates

INV_processing places trees without coordinates at random within their
subplot or plot, in each AGB simulation. This increases the uncertainty of
quadrat AGB density, especially where large trees are unmapped. Trees where
no stems have coordinates are listed below:

```{r}
# Trees where no stems have coordinates, with their number of stems and basal
# area
tree_key <- do.call(paste, s_focal[, id_tree])
has_xy <- !is.na(s_focal$x_rel_m) & !is.na(s_focal$y_rel_m)
unmapped <- !tree_key %in% tree_key[has_xy]
df_treeUnmapped <- aggregate(
  list(n_stem = rep(1, sum(unmapped)), 
    ba_m2 = pi * (s_focal$diam_cm[unmapped] / 200)^2), 
  by = s_focal[unmapped, id_tree], FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)

showFlags(df_treeUnmapped)
```

Plot the percentage of basal area in each plot in unmapped trees:

```{r}
ba_plot <- aggregate(list(ba_m2 = pi * (s_focal$diam_cm / 200)^2), 
  by = list(plot_id = s_focal$plot_id), FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
ba_unmapped <- aggregate(list(ba_m2_unmapped = df_treeUnmapped$ba_m2), 
  by = list(plot_id = df_treeUnmapped$plot_id), FUN = sum)
ba_plot <- merge(ba_plot, ba_unmapped, all.x = TRUE)
ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped[is.na(ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped)] <- 0
ba_plot$pct_unmapped <- 100 * ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped / ba_plot$ba_m2

ggplot(ba_plot, aes(x = plot_id, y = pct_unmapped)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of basal area in unmapped trees") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Coordinates of multi-stemmed trees

The stems of a multi-stemmed tree should be close to each other. Trees where
any two stems are more than 5 m apart may have wrong stem coordinates, or
stems assigned to the wrong tree:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagMultiLoc)
```

```{r}
df_flagMultiLoc <- flagMultiLoc(
  x = s_focal,
  ind_id = id_tree,
  census_id = "census_id",
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  threshold = tree_stem_dist_max_m,
  comment = "Multi-stemmed tree with incongruous stem coordinates"
)

showFlags(df_flagMultiLoc)
```

### Tree and stem IDs

INV_processing combines the stems of each tree into a single equivalent
diameter to estimate AGB, and assigns the tree to a quadrat using the centroid
of its stems. The stems of a tree should normally be in the same subplot:

```{r}
# Trees with stems in more than one subplot
tree_sub <- aggregate(subplot_id ~ site_id + plot_id + tree_id, data = s_focal, 
  FUN = function(i) { paste(unique(i), collapse = "; ") })
df_treeMultiSubplot <- tree_sub[grepl("; ", tree_sub$subplot_id), ]

showFlags(df_treeMultiSubplot)
```

Trees with very many stems may be several trees which have been given the
same tree ID. Trees with more than `tree_stem_max` stems are listed below:

```{r}
tree_n <- aggregate(list(n_stem = rep(1, nrow(s_focal))), by = s_focal[, id_tree], FUN = sum)
df_treeManyStems <- tree_n[tree_n$n_stem > tree_stem_max, ]

showFlags(df_treeManyStems)
```

## Taxonomic name issues 

### Basic orthographic and nomenclature issues

Taxonomic names should only contain letters and spaces, and family names
should end in "-aceae". Names with other characters, e.g. "?" or ".", or
genus and species names ending in "-aceae", may not be matched to the World
Flora Online database by INV_processing:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTaxonName)
```

```{r}
df_flagTaxonName <- flagTaxonName(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  taxon_name = "taxon_name",
  family = NULL, 
  genus = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  regex = "[^a-zA-Z ]",
  comment = "Taxonomic name issue"
)

showFlags(df_flagTaxonName)
```

### Taxonomic resolution

Stems which are not identified to species have their wood density estimated
at genus, family or plot level by INV_processing, which increases the
uncertainty of their AGB estimates. If you have morphospecies codes, check
that they are consistently formatted, e.g. "Brachystegia sp1" rather than a
mix of "Brachystegia sp1" and "Brachystegia sp. 1".

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTaxonLevel)
```

```{r}
df_flagTaxonLevel <- flagTaxonLevel(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  taxon_name = "taxon_name",
  comment = "Stem not identified to species"
)

showFlags(df_flagTaxonLevel)
```

Plot the percentage of live basal area at each taxonomic level in each plot:

```{r}
s_lev <- merge(s_focal, df_flagTaxonLevel[, c(id_meas, "taxon_level")], all.x = TRUE)
s_lev$taxon_level[is.na(s_lev$taxon_level)] <- "species"
s_lev$ba_m2 <- pi * (s_lev$diam_cm / 200)^2
s_lev <- s_lev[grepl("A", s_lev$code) & !is.na(s_lev$ba_m2), ]

ggplot(s_lev, aes(x = plot_id, weight = ba_m2, fill = taxon_level)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of live basal area", fill = "Taxonomic level") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Alternative growth forms

Palms, tree ferns, bamboos and other plants which are not dicot or conifer
trees should be labelled in `growth_form`. INV_processing can assign an
alternative allometry to these stems with `agb_allometry`, e.g.
"goodman2013" for palms, or exclude them from AGB density with
`growth_form_exclude`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagFormAlt)
```

```{r}
df_flagFormAlt <- flagFormAlt(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  taxon_name = "taxon_name",
  family = NULL,  # Provide a family column if available, e.g. from `tx`
  growth_form = "growth_form",
  comment = "Possible alternative growth form"
)

showFlags(df_flagFormAlt)
```

### Taxonomic names of multi-stemmed trees

All stems of a tree should have the same taxonomic name. INV_processing uses
the wood density of the largest stem of each tree:

```{r}
# Trees with stems with different taxonomic names
tree_taxa <- aggregate(taxon_name ~ site_id + plot_id + tree_id, data = s_focal, 
  FUN = function(i) { paste(unique(i), collapse = "; ") })
df_treeMultiTaxon <- tree_taxa[grepl("; ", tree_taxa$taxon_name), ]

showFlags(df_treeMultiTaxon)
```

### Check taxonomic names against the World Flora Online database

INV_processing matches taxonomic names to the World Flora Online database with
`BIOMASS::correctTaxo()`. Check names which are changed or not matched below,
and correct them in the stem measurement table if necessary. Matching needs an
internet connection:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctTaxo, pkg = "BIOMASS")
```

```{r}
# The World Flora Online API is occasionally unavailable. If so, the rest of
# the notebook still runs, and this chunk can be run again later.
# `suppressMessages()` hides the progress bar
df_correctTaxo <- tryCatch(suppressMessages(
  BIOMASS::correctTaxo(
    unique(s_focal$taxon_name),
    interactive = FALSE,
    preferAccepted = TRUE,
    preferFuzzy = TRUE,
    sub_pattern = BIOMASS::subPattern(),
    useCache = FALSE,
    useAPI = TRUE,
    capacity = 60,
    fill_time_s = 60,
    timeout = 10)),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("Taxonomic name matching failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    NULL
  })

if (!is.null(df_correctTaxo)) {
  showFlags(unique(df_correctTaxo[df_correctTaxo$nameModified == TRUE,]))
}
```

### Wood density

INV_processing estimates wood density at the finest taxonomic level
available in the Global Wood Density Database, falling back to genus, family,
and finally the plot mean. Stems with genus, family or plot mean wood density
have more uncertain AGB estimates.

```{r}
# Estimate wood density for stems in all censuses, used below
taxon_genus <- sub(" .*", "", trimws(s$taxon_name))
taxon_species <- ifelse(grepl(" ", trimws(s$taxon_name)), 
  sub("^\\S+\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", trimws(s$taxon_name)), NA_character_)
wd_est <- BIOMASS::getWoodDensity(
  genus = taxon_genus, 
  species = taxon_species, 
  stand = s$plot_id, 
  verbose = FALSE)
s$wd_gcm3 <- wd_est$meanWD
s$wd_level <- ifelse(wd_est$levelWD %in% c("species", "genus", "family"), 
  wd_est$levelWD, "plot mean")
```

Plot the percentage of live basal area at each wood density level in each
plot:

```{r}
s_wd <- s[s$focal & grepl("A", s$code) & !is.na(s$diam_cm), ]

ggplot(s_wd, aes(x = plot_id, weight = diam_cm^2, 
  fill = factor(wd_level, levels = c("species", "genus", "family", "plot mean")))) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of live basal area", fill = "Wood density level") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

If you have provided local wood density measurements, check that values are
within the range of the Global Wood Density Database, which is used by
INV_processing for taxa without local measurements:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Wood density outside the range of the Global Wood Density Database (g cm-3)
df_wdRange <- wd[wd$wood_density_gcm3 < 0.08 | wd$wood_density_gcm3 > 1.39, ]

showFlags(df_wdRange)
```

## Preview of AGB estimates

### Stems used to estimate AGB

Preview which stem measurements INV_processing will exclude from AGB
estimates and AGB density, and why. Check that stems are excluded for the
right reasons. For example, live standing stems which are excluded because
they have no code, or many stems excluded as "not standing", may indicate
errors in the `code` column.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagAgbExclude)
```

```{r}
df_flagAgbExclude <- flagAgbExclude(
  x = s_focal,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  tree_id = "tree_id",
  stem_id = "stem_id",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  code = "code",
  pom = "pom_m",
  date = "measurement_date",
  plot = p,
  plot_diam_min = "meas_diam_min_cm",
  growth_form = "growth_form",
  missing_diam = inv_missing_diam_impute,
  include_broken = inv_include_broken,
  agbd_diam_min_cm = inv_agbd_diam_min_cm,
  growth_form_exclude = inv_growth_form_exclude,
  comment = "Stem excluded from AGB estimates"
)

showFlags(df_flagAgbExclude)
```

Plot the number of stem records excluded for each reason in each plot:

```{r}
ggplot(df_flagAgbExclude, aes(x = plot_id, fill = reason)) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Number of stem records", fill = NULL) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

### Approximate AGB

To see which stems and plots will dominate AGB density, estimate the AGB of
each stem with the Chave et al. (2014) allometry, using the wood density
estimated above, and the location of each plot, as with `height_method:
"regional"` in INV_processing. These estimates are only approximate:
INV_processing combines the stems of multi-stemmed trees, propagates
uncertainty, and may use different height and wood density methods.

Calculate the longitude and latitude of the centre of each plot from its
corners. The Chave et al. (2014) allometry uses plot location to account for
regional differences in tree height:

```{r}
pt_cent <- aggregate(
  cbind(x = rover_easting_utm_m, y = rover_northing_utm_m) ~ plot_id + crs_epsg, 
  data = pt, FUN = mean)
plot_ll <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pt_cent, pt_cent$crs_epsg), function(y) {
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(
    sf::st_as_sf(y, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = as.integer(y$crs_epsg[1])), 4326))
  data.frame(plot_id = y$plot_id, longitude = xy[, 1], latitude = xy[, 2])
}))

ggplot(plot_ll, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, label = plot_id)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(nudge_y = 0.002, size = 3) + 
  coord_quickmap() + 
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
```

Estimate the AGB of live, standing stems with a diameter, in all censuses.
These estimates are also used in [Part II](#part-ii-multi-census-checks-of-the-focal-census):

```{r}
s$agb_inc <- grepl("A", s$code) & grepl("S", s$code) & 
  !grepl("[TM]", s$code) & !is.na(s$diam_cm)
coord <- as.matrix(plot_ll[match(s$plot_id, plot_ll$plot_id), 
  c("longitude", "latitude")])
s$agb_Mg <- NA_real_
s$agb_Mg[s$agb_inc] <- BIOMASS::computeAGB(
  D = s$diam_cm[s$agb_inc], 
  WD = s$wd_gcm3[s$agb_inc], 
  coord = coord[s$agb_inc, , drop = FALSE])
s$ba_m2 <- pi * (s$diam_cm / 200)^2
s_focal <- s[s$focal, ]
```

Plot stem AGB against diameter. Points far from the main cloud may be errors
in diameter or wood density:

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(s_focal[s_focal$agb_inc, ], aes(x = diam_cm, y = agb_Mg, colour = wd_level)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  scale_x_log10() + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Stem AGB (Mg)", colour = "Wood density level")
```

Plot the share of plot AGB in each 10 cm diameter class. Plots where a few
large stems hold most of the AGB are most sensitive to errors in the
measurements of those stems:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
sf_agb <- s_focal[s_focal$agb_inc, ]
sf_agb$diam_class <- cut(sf_agb$diam_cm, breaks = seq(0, 10 * ceiling(max(sf_agb$diam_cm) / 10), 10))

ggplot(sf_agb, aes(x = diam_class, weight = agb_Mg)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = 1), fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Diameter class (cm)", y = "Percentage of plot AGB") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

Calculate the approximate AGB density of each plot, using the plot
dimensions in the plot meta-data table. Check that AGB density is plausible
for the vegetation type of each plot:

```{r}
agbd <- aggregate(list(agb_Mg = s_focal$agb_Mg), by = list(plot_id = s_focal$plot_id), 
  FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
agbd$area_ha <- with(p[match(agbd$plot_id, p$plot_id), ],
  plot_length_m * plot_width_m / 10000)
agbd$agbd_Mg_ha <- agbd$agb_Mg / agbd$area_ha

datatable(agbd)

ggplot(agbd, aes(x = reorder(plot_id, agbd_Mg_ha), y = agbd_Mg_ha)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = expression("Approximate AGB density (Mg ha"^-1*")")) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Part II: Multi-census checks of the focal census

__This part of the notebook should only be used if you have access to
multi-census data.__

The checks in this part are run on data from all censuses, `s`, and can find
issues in any census. The results are then merged with the IDs of stems or
measurements in the focal census, `s_focal`, e.g. `merge(df_all, unique(s_focal[, 
id_stem]))`, to keep only the issues which affect the focal census. Issues in
all censuses are kept in objects ending `_all`, which you may wish to inspect,
but they do not need to be fixed for INV_processing.

Several functions in this part need the mortality status of each stem
measurement as a logical column. Stems with "D" in `code` are dead, stems
with "A" are alive, and stems with neither are `NA`, i.e. status unknown:

```{r}
s$alive <- NA
s$alive[grepl("A", s$code)] <- TRUE
s$alive[grepl("D", s$code)] <- FALSE
```

## Data overview

Plot the number of stem records in each plot census. Large differences in the
number of records among censuses of the same plot may indicate that part of a
plot was not measured, or that records are missing from the data:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(s, aes(x = plot_id, fill = factor(census_id))) + 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", aes(colour = focal)) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "black", "FALSE" = NA), guide = "none") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Number of stem records", fill = "Census") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Plot the composition of stem codes in each plot census. A sudden change in
the focal census may indicate a change in field protocol or data entry errors:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(s, aes(x = factor(census_id), fill = code)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Census", y = "Percentage of stem records", fill = "Code")
```

## Stems missing from the focal census

Stems which were alive in a previous census should be recorded in the focal
census, either with a new measurement, as dead, or as missing ("M"). Stems
with no record in the focal census may have been missed in the field or lost
during data entry.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecordAbsent)
```

```{r}
df_flagRecordAbsent <- flagRecordAbsent(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  status = "alive",
  focal = s$focal,
  comment = "Stem alive previously, absent from focal census"
)

showFlags(df_flagRecordAbsent)
```

`flagRecordMissing()` finds stems recorded before and after a census, but not
in that census. Missing records should be added to the stem measurement
table.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecordMissing)
```

```{r}
df_flagRecordMissing_all <- flagRecordMissing(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_id_vec = NULL,  # Optional vector of census IDs
  plot_id = id_plot,  # Guess census IDs separately for each plot
  comment = "Missing stem measurement record"
)

df_flagRecordMissing <- merge(df_flagRecordMissing_all, 
  unique(s_focal[, c(id_plot, "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_flagRecordMissing)
```

## Stem IDs among censuses

Stem IDs should be unique within a plot, so each stem should only ever belong
to one tree, in every census:

```{r}
# Stems which belong to more than one tree, in any census
stem_tree <- aggregate(tree_id ~ site_id + plot_id + stem_id, data = s, 
  FUN = function(i) { paste(unique(i), collapse = "; ") })
df_stemMultiTree_all <- stem_tree[grepl("; ", stem_tree$tree_id), ]

# Stems in the focal census
df_stemMultiTree <- merge(df_stemMultiTree_all, unique(s_focal[, c(id_plot, "stem_id")]))

showFlags(df_stemMultiTree)
```

## Plot-level change

Compare the total basal area, number of live stems, and AGB of each plot to
the previous census of the plot. Annual changes greater than
`change_ann_max` are flagged.
Large changes in plot totals may indicate that part of the plot was not
measured, that stems were duplicated, that diameters are in the wrong units,
or that a disturbance event occurred, which should be described in the plot
meta-data table.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPlotChange)
```

```{r}
# Live standing stems
live <- grepl("A", s$code) & !grepl("[FM]", s$code)

df_flagPlotChange_ba_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = "ba_m2",
  cond = live,
  threshold = change_ann_max,
  comment = "Large change in plot basal area"
)

df_flagPlotChange_n_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = NULL,
  cond = live,
  threshold = change_ann_max,
  comment = "Large change in plot stem density"
)

df_flagPlotChange_agb_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = "agb_Mg",
  cond = s$agb_inc,
  threshold = change_ann_max,
  comment = "Large change in plot AGB"
)

# Changes since the previous census in the focal census
df_flagPlotChange <- merge(rbind(
  df_flagPlotChange_ba_all, 
  df_flagPlotChange_n_all, 
  df_flagPlotChange_agb_all), unique(s_focal[, c(id_plot, "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_flagPlotChange)
```

Plot the totals of each plot over time, with the focal census filled red:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
plot_ts <- aggregate(
  list(
    ba_m2 = ifelse(live, s$ba_m2, 0),
    n_stem = as.numeric(live),
    agb_Mg = ifelse(s$agb_inc, s$agb_Mg, 0)),
  by = list(plot_id = s$plot_id, census_id = s$census_id, focal = s$focal,
    census_date = decYear(s$census_date)),
  FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
plot_ts_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")],
    metric = "Basal area (m2)", value = plot_ts$ba_m2),
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")],
    metric = "Live stems", value = plot_ts$n_stem),
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")],
    metric = "AGB (Mg)", value = plot_ts$agb_Mg))

ggplot(plot_ts_long, aes(x = census_date, y = value, group = plot_id)) + 
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 2) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Census date", y = NULL, fill = "Focal census")
```

The same check within subplots can find subplots which were missed, or
measured twice:

```{r}
df_flagPlotChange_subplot_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = c(id_plot, "subplot_id"),
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = NULL,
  cond = live,
  threshold = change_ann_max_subplot,
  comment = "Large change in subplot stem density"
)

df_flagPlotChange_subplot <- merge(df_flagPlotChange_subplot_all, 
  unique(s_focal[, c(id_plot, "subplot_id", "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_flagPlotChange_subplot)
```

Plot the number of live stems in each subplot in each census. Subplots with
far fewer or far more stems in the focal census than in other censuses may
have been missed, or measured twice:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
sub_n <- aggregate(list(n_stem = as.numeric(live)), 
  by = list(plot_id = s$plot_id, subplot_id = s$subplot_id, 
    census_id = s$census_id), FUN = sum)

ggplot(sub_n, aes(x = factor(census_id), y = factor(subplot_id), fill = n_stem)) + 
  geom_tile() + 
  geom_text(aes(label = n_stem), size = 2.5) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free") + 
  labs(x = "Census", y = "Subplot", fill = "Live stems")
```

## Mortality and recruitment

Annual mortality and recruitment rates in old-growth forests are typically
1-3%. Census intervals ending in the focal census with rates greater than
`demog_rate_max` are flagged. High mortality may indicate stems which were missed or retagged.
High recruitment may indicate stems which were missed in the previous census,
a change in the minimum diameter threshold, or retagged stems.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagDemogRate)
```

```{r}
df_flagDemogRate_all <- flagDemogRate(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  status = "alive",
  threshold = demog_rate_max,
  comment = "High mortality or recruitment rate"
)

# Intervals ending in the focal census
df_flagDemogRate <- df_flagDemogRate_all[
  paste(df_flagDemogRate_all$plot_id, df_flagDemogRate_all$census_t1) %in% 
    paste(s_focal$plot_id, s_focal$census_id), ]

showFlags(df_flagDemogRate)
```

Plot the mortality and recruitment rates of all census intervals, with
intervals ending in the focal census filled red:

```{r}
demog <- suppressMessages(flagDemogRate(s, id_stem, id_plot, "census_id", 
  "census_date", "alive", threshold = -Inf))
demog$focal <- paste(demog$plot_id, demog$census_t1) %in% 
  paste(s_focal$plot_id, s_focal$census_id)
demog_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(demog[, c("plot_id", "census_t1", "focal")], 
    rate = "Mortality", value = demog$mort_ann),
  data.frame(demog[, c("plot_id", "census_t1", "focal")], 
    rate = "Recruitment", value = demog$recr_ann))

ggplot(demog_long, aes(x = plot_id, y = 100 * value)) + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 2.5) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100 * demog_rate_max, linetype = 2) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  facet_wrap(~rate, ncol = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Annual rate (%)", fill = "Ends in focal census") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Retagged stems

A stem which disappears between censuses, and a recruit with a similar
diameter at almost the same location, may be the same stem with a new tag.
Retagged stems inflate mortality and recruitment rates, and break diameter
timelines, so that errors in the focal census cannot be found from previous
censuses:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTagChange)
```

```{r}
df_flagTagChange_all <- flagTagChange(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  status = "alive",
  threshold = tag_dist_max_m,
  diam_tol = tag_diam_tol,
  comment = "Recruit may be a retagged stem"
)

# Recruits in the focal census
df_flagTagChange <- merge(df_flagTagChange_all, unique(s_focal[, c(id_stem, "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_flagTagChange)
```

## Diameter timeline

Calculate the annual diameter growth of live stems between consecutive
censuses, where the POM did not change:

```{r}
g <- s[grepl("A", s$code) & !is.na(s$diam_cm), 
  c(id_stem, "census_id", "census_date", "diam_cm", "pom_m", "focal")]
g$date <- decYear(g$census_date)
g <- g[do.call(order, g[, c(id_stem, "date")]), ]
g_key <- do.call(paste, g[, id_stem])
same <- c(FALSE, g_key[-1] == g_key[-length(g_key)]) & 
  c(FALSE, g$pom_m[-1] == g$pom_m[-nrow(g)]) %in% TRUE
g$diam_prev <- ifelse(same, c(NA, g$diam_cm[-nrow(g)]), NA)
g$growth_cm_yr <- ifelse(same, 
  (g$diam_cm - g$diam_prev) / (g$date - c(NA, g$date[-nrow(g)])), NA)
g <- g[!is.na(g$growth_cm_yr), ]
```

Plot growth against diameter in the previous census. The dashed lines show
the growth thresholds used by `correctDiameterSeries()` below. Implausibly
fast growth or shrinkage indicates an error in one of the two diameter
measurements:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(g, aes(x = diam_prev, y = growth_cm_yr, colour = focal)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(growth_min_cm_yr, growth_max_cm_yr), linetype = 2) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey50")) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Diameter in previous census (cm)", 
    y = expression("Diameter growth (cm y"^-1*")"), 
    colour = "Ends in focal census")
```

Stems with growth outside the thresholds between the previous census and the
focal census are listed below. This includes stems with only two censuses,
where `correctDiameterSeries()` cannot tell which of the two diameters is
wrong:

```{r}
df_growthRange <- g[g$focal & 
  (g$growth_cm_yr < growth_min_cm_yr | g$growth_cm_yr > growth_max_cm_yr), 
  c(id_stem, "census_id", "diam_prev", "diam_cm", "growth_cm_yr")]

showFlags(df_growthRange)
```

`correctDiameterSeries()` finds diameter measurements which are
inconsistent with the rest of the diameter timeline of each stem, and
suggests corrected values. Corrected diameters are suggestions. Check the
field data sheets for each stem before changing diameters in the focal
census.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctDiameterSeries)
```

```{r}
df_correctDiameterSeries_all <- correctDiameterSeries(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_date = "census_date",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  status = "alive",
  pom = "pom_m",
  growth_thresh = c(growth_min_cm_yr, growth_max_cm_yr),
  n_stem_thresh = 3, 
  digits = 1,
  method = c("shift", "pairwise"),
  shift_anchor = "longest",  # Majority of the diameter timeline is correct
  comment = "Diameter timelines corrected"
)

# Corrections to measurements in the focal census
df_correctDiameterSeries <- merge(df_correctDiameterSeries_all, 
  unique(s_focal[, c(id_stem, "census_date")]))

showFlags(df_correctDiameterSeries)
```

Plot the diameter timelines of the stems with the largest corrections in
the focal census:

```{r}
cor_top <- df_correctDiameterSeries[
  order(-abs(df_correctDiameterSeries$diam_cor - df_correctDiameterSeries$diam_cm)), ]
cor_top <- cor_top[!is.na(cor_top$diam_cm), ][seq_len(min(6, nrow(cor_top))), ]

if (nrow(cor_top) > 0) {
  cor_plots <- plotDiameterCorrections(s, cor_top, id_stem, "census_date", 
    "diam_cm", pom = "pom_m")
  for (i in cor_plots) {
    print(i)
  }
}
```

## Mortality timeline

`correctMortalitySeries()` finds inconsistent mortality status timelines, e.g.
a stem recorded as dead and then alive again, and missing mortality status,
and suggests corrections. Check the field data sheets for each stem before
changing codes in the focal census.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctMortalitySeries)
```

```{r}
df_correctMortalitySeries_all <- correctMortalitySeries(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  census_id = "census_id",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  status = "alive",
  comment = "Mortality timelines corrected"
)

# Corrections to measurements in the focal census
df_correctMortalitySeries <- merge(
  df_correctMortalitySeries_all[!is.na(df_correctMortalitySeries_all$method), ], 
  unique(s_focal[, c(id_stem, "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_correctMortalitySeries)
```

## Stem condition timeline

Some changes in stem condition between censuses are impossible, e.g. a dead
stem becoming alive, or a fallen stem standing again. Stems which are broken
above or below the POM should remain broken in later censuses:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagCodeSeries)
```

```{r}
df_flagCodeSeries_all <- flagCodeSeries(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  census_id = "census_id",
  target = "code",
  invalid_trans = list(
    c("D", "A"),
    c("F", "S"),
    c("B", NA_character_),
    c("T", NA_character_)
  ),
  comment = "Invalid code transition"
)

# Stems in the focal census
df_flagCodeSeries <- merge(df_flagCodeSeries_all, unique(s_focal[, id_stem]))

showFlags(df_flagCodeSeries)
```

## Taxonomy timeline

A stem should normally have the same taxonomic name in every census. Where
taxonomic names differ among censuses, the name in the focal census is not
necessarily wrong, e.g. if a stem was re-identified by a specialist:

```{r}
# Stems with different taxonomic names in different censuses
stem_taxa <- aggregate(taxon_name ~ site_id + plot_id + tree_id + stem_id, 
  data = s, FUN = function(i) { paste(unique(i), collapse = "; ") })
df_taxonSeries_all <- stem_taxa[grepl("; ", stem_taxa$taxon_name), ]

# Stems in the focal census
df_taxonSeries <- merge(df_taxonSeries_all, unique(s_focal[, id_stem]))

showFlags(df_taxonSeries)
```

## Location timeline

Stem coordinates should not change much between censuses. Stems which move by
more than `loc_change_max_m` may have wrong coordinates in one census, which affects the
quadrat they are assigned to in INV_processing:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagLocSeries)
```

```{r}
df_flagLocSeries_all <- flagLocSeries(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  census_id = "census_id",
  threshold = loc_change_max_m,
  comment = "Stem location differs among censuses"
)

# Stems in the focal census
df_flagLocSeries <- merge(df_flagLocSeries_all, unique(s_focal[, id_stem]))

showFlags(df_flagLocSeries)
```

## Overgrown recruits

Recruits are stems recorded for the first time. A recruit in the focal census
which is much larger than it could have grown from the minimum diameter
threshold since the previous census was probably missed in the previous
census:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecruitBig)
```

```{r}
df_flagRecruitBig_all <- flagRecruitBig(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  diam = "diam_cm",
  census_date = "census_date",
  plot = p,
  plot_diam_min = "meas_diam_min_cm",
  growth_max = recruit_growth_max_cm_yr,
  comment = "Overgrown recruit"
)

# Recruits in the focal census
df_flagRecruitBig <- merge(df_flagRecruitBig_all, 
  unique(s_focal[, c(id_stem, "census_date")]))

showFlags(df_flagRecruitBig)
```

## Pre-recorded recruits

Stems whose first record has no diameter may have been back-filled in the
data to censuses before they were recruited:

```{r}
s_ord <- s[order(s$census_id), ]
s_first <- s_ord[!duplicated(s_ord[, id_stem]), ]
df_recruitPre_all <- s_first[is.na(s_first$diam_cm), 
  c(id_stem, "census_id", "code", "diam_cm")]

# First records in the focal census
df_recruitPre <- merge(df_recruitPre_all, unique(s_focal[, c(id_stem, "census_id")]))

showFlags(df_recruitPre)
```

```{r}
saveRDS(flag_list, "./flag_list.rds")
```

Summarise the number of records flagged by each check. Issues which stop
INV_processing must be fixed before the focal census is submitted: errors in
the format of the tables, plots missing from the plot meta-data or
geo-location tables, duplicated records, missing IDs or codes, invalid codes,
and measurements recorded on missing stems. Other issues should be reviewed,
and fixed where they are errors:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
must_fix <- c("checkTableSpec_stem", "checkTableSpec_plot", "checkTableSpec_pt",
  "plotMissing", "ptMissing", "recordDup", "valMissing", "flagCodeVal",
  "valPresentMissing")

flag_summ <- data.frame(
  check = names(flag_list),
  n_flagged = sapply(flag_list, NROW))
flag_summ$action <- ifelse(flag_summ$check %in% must_fix, "Must fix", "Review")
flag_summ <- flag_summ[order(flag_summ$action, -flag_summ$n_flagged), ]

datatable(flag_summ, rownames = FALSE)

ggplot(flag_summ[flag_summ$n_flagged > 0, ],
  aes(x = n_flagged, y = reorder(check, n_flagged), fill = action)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Must fix" = "red", "Review" = "grey")) +
  labs(x = "Number of rows flagged", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

Write the focal census stem measurement table to submit to INV_processing,
with only the columns in the INV_processing specification, and check it
again. There should be no "error" rows before the focal census is submitted:

```{r}
stem_cols <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/main/templates/stem_cols.csv", 
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")

s_out <- s_focal[, intersect(stem_cols$column_name, names(s_focal))]

df_checkTableSpec_out <- checkTableSpec(s_out, stem_cols)
showFlags(df_checkTableSpec_out)

write.csv(s_out, "./stem_focal.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
